catalog_citation: Barham, R. Marie. 1958. The phonemes of the Buhid (Mangyan) language of Eastern Mindoro, Philippines. In: Studies in Philippine Linguistics by members of the Summer Institute of Linguistics (Pacific Branch), Oceania Linguistic Monographs No. 3, pp. 4-9. Unive…
catalog_locator: p. 9, section 5 'Stress' (PDF page 6 of 7); also section 6 'Vowel Length', p. 9
catalog_quote: 5. Stress. Stress is contrastive, as shown by the following examples: /ʔédo/ 'dog'; /rírok/ 'write'; /ŋáyan/ 'name'; /bákbaŋ/ 'wooden bar'; /buhágod/ 'proud'; /tabó/ 'end'; /namók/ 'mosquito'; /tagán/ 'nest of domestic fowl'; /kapsán/ 'beside'; /ʔʌbʌsʌ́d/ 'deep'. Words ending in an open syllable have a predominant pattern of penultimate stress, as shown by the following examples: /bágo/ 'new'; /ʔídya/ 'not yet'; /hʌ́tsi/ 'there'; /kalímo/ 'startle'; /ʔalfóyo/ 'head'. ... 6. Vowel Length ... As yet, no contrast in length has been observed in words of Buhid origin, although at times the vowels in certain stressed syllables appear to be somewhat longer than comparable vowels in unstressed syllables.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote: confirmed verbatim on the page image we hold (Barham 1958 p. 9, sections 5-6); locator and strength of the evidence 'page-image' are correct (scanned layer is garbled there). (2) Deciding source: a 1958 six-page SIL phonemic sketch -- old and brief, but it is the sole descriptive work on Buhid in Glottolog (1 ref) and the only phonology of the language found by web search (SIL archive, OLAC, Wikipedia refs: Barham 1958, Barbian 1977 vocabulary, Pennoyer 1979 subgrouping; UP Diliman 2022 word list). So the best available source is held and quoted. (3) New evidence downloaded: Zorc 1979 (PL C-45:243-4) groups Buhid with Kuyonon/Tausug/Gaddang as languages that 'do not reflect PPH accent' -- a passing comparative claim (no data) that inherited contrastive accent was not continued. sources.citation: Zorc, R. David. 1979. On the development of contrastive word accent: Pangasinan, a case in point. In Nguyen Dang Liem (ed.), South-East Asian Linguistic Studies Vol. 3, 241-258. Pacific Linguistics C-45. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: 'Since there are other Philippine languages that do not reflect PPH accent, e.g. Kuyonon and Tausug within Bisayan (Zorc 1977), Buhid within South Mangyan, Gaddang within Banagic, etc., it is therefore plausible that Png independently lost contrastive accent in cognate forms.' One-line comparative remark; no Buhid forms or synchronic stress rule given.

sources.note: Second linguist with Buhid field data (Pennoyer worked on neighbouring Tawbuid, which has non-contrastive stress); a subgrouping paper that may state whether Buhid shares Tawbuid's loss of contrastive accent, which would settle between Barham 1958 ('stress is contrastive') and Zorc 1979's remark that Buhid 'does not reflect PPH accent'.
